nodes.description: Cerebellar dysplasia or volume loss, dilated ventricles, corpus callosum hypoplasia or agenesis and pontine hypoplasia are common, occasionally with rhombencephalosynapsis. They resemble the brain phenotype of ZIC1 loss of function, suggesting the final-exon variants also reduce ZIC1 function in the brain, and they arise independently of suture fusion. The intellectual disability, developmental delay and autism are treated as expressions of the same disordered neurodevelopment; their relation to the structural anomalies is unstudied.

nodes.description: Coronal suture progenitors are mesoderm cells that gather above the eye (the supraorbital regulatory center) and migrate apically to form the suture, a step that needs engrailed 1. Mouse Zic1 is expressed there at E11.5 to E12.5, overlapping En1. The model proposes that altered ZIC1 disturbs this step; it rests on expression timing and En1 genetics and has not been tested in an animal carrying a final-exon variant.
